subtitulo: An empty school given back to the town
texto: The work starts from a building that has lost its use and sets out to give it a new one. The place is Urnieta, and the chosen complex is the ikastola where I studied: it has outgrown itself and is being moved to a new building, so the site is drifting towards emptiness.
Looking at it closely and seeing how many problems it carries, the brief grew: not only the building but the whole site is woven back into the town, through refurbishment, renovation and extension.
The new uses start from what the town currently lacks, and address residents and visitors alike, with the well-being of the town today and in the future as the ground to stand on.

subtitulo: Three housing blocks to bring people back to a hill village
texto: Astigarreta is a small cluster of buildings up in the hills, in the Goierri district. The brief asked for three housing blocks that would fit their surroundings, alert to the state the village is in and to how new homes might help repopulate the area by encouraging community life.

What this project teaches has to do with organising the terrain. The mountainous topography of the Basque Country leaves small villages cut off from the towns, and that connection can only be solved with the transport that already exists. So the project concentrates on what is within its reach: making homes and public space, fitting the street, the squares and the buildings to the neighbours there are and the ones who might come.

subtitulo: A playground by the school that serves the whole village
texto: A redevelopment project in a small Polish village, next to a school that has no playground of its own.

The brief is read at two scales from the outset: solving the yard the school needs and, through the same move, giving the whole village the public space it lacks. What is built for the children during school hours stays available to the neighbours the rest of the time.
The work begins with an analysis of the area — routes, uses and references — and it is that analysis that ends up setting where to intervene and how hard.

subtitulo: A brick ruin turned into a cultural space
texto: The brief was to give new life to a church abandoned after the Second World War, in the town of Gubin, Poland. The church stands in complete ruin: only the columns, the façade and the central tower remain, all of them in brick.

The reconstruction reuses and completes the authentic structure of its time with a new, self-supporting one that stays distinct from the original and brings it up to date. As for its use, the original function is weighed against present-day needs, and what comes out is a generous cultural space joining history and today: concerts, exhibitions and somewhere for visitors to rest.
What matters here is understanding what is already there, and making it evolve and adapt to time without changing what it is.

subtitulo: Market, public facilities and housing at the Magdalena bastion
texto: The project sits at the Magdalena bastion in Hondarribia, right where the old town meets the nineteenth-century extension. Understanding how people move across that seam is the key to everything else.

The brief asked for a market, administrative facilities, offices, a multipurpose cultural hall and sheltered housing for independent older people, and at the same time for relocating the gastronomic society and the woodwork shop that were getting in the way.

The answer is three blocks: a small one for the market, a central one holding culture and administration and carrying the weight of the place, and a third turned into a housing building. Each is given the position where it works.

subtitulo: Blocks of differing shape tuned to climate and terrain
texto: The project sits in Elorrieta, an industrial district of Bilbao, and called for a development that would fit the shape and the topography of the area.

It proposes a play of blocks of differing shape and height. The composition was tested with Envimet, which makes it possible to justify the shadows, the air currents and the temperatures reached over the year.
What this teaches is how to use different volumes and get them, together, to form a whole that works and fits the brief.
